cards.explanation: The answer is thanksgiving songs with cymbals and harps. The verse says the Levites came "…to celebrate the joyous dedication with thanksgiving and singing, accompanied by cymbals, harps, and lyres." Cymbals, harps AND lyres, friends. That's a whole lineup for one celebration.

The word is purify. Verse 30 says, "After the priests and Levites had purified themselves, they purified the people, the gates, and the wall." They started with themselves, then moved on to everything else. That's like me wiping off my mustache before I touch the dough.

The first choir marches along the top of the wall. Nehemiah says, "…I brought the leaders of Judah up on the wall…" and the first choir was to "…proceed along the top of the wall to the right…" Up high, right on top of the wall. I'd have wanted that view myself.

The answer is the Dung Gate. Verse 31 says the first choir was to proceed along the top of the wall "…to the right, toward the Dung Gate." Nehemiah appointed that choir to go that direction, so that's the gate to remember.

The answer is David. Verse 36 says the instruments were "…prescribed by David the man of God." The text gives David that title right there. Zechariah and his associates were playing with the instruments David prescribed.
The answer is False. Verse 36 says, "Ezra the scribe led the procession." So Ezra was up front with the first choir. Nehemiah was off following the second choir (Nehemiah 12:38).

The answer is half the people. Nehemiah says, "…I followed it with half the people along the top of the wall…" The first group had half the leaders, and this one had half the people. Imagine the noise of all that marching on a wall.

The word is house. Verse 40 says, "The two thanksgiving choirs then stood in the house of God…" They headed off in opposite directions and ended up in the same place, like two bakers who take different routes and meet at the same cooling rack.

The reason is that God had given them great joy. Verse 43 says they offered great sacrifices, "…rejoicing because God had given them great joy." The joy came from God, so that's where the credit goes.
The answer is False. Verse 43 says, "The women and children also rejoiced…" It wasn't a men-only party. The text says it was "…so that the joy of Jerusalem was heard from afar."
The answer is that it was heard from afar. Verse 43 says the joy of Jerusalem "…was heard from afar." It didn't stay in one spot. People far from the city could hear it.

The reason is that they rejoiced over the priests and Levites serving. Verse 44 says the portions were gathered "…because Judah rejoiced over the priests and Levites who were serving." The people were glad about the service, and that's why they brought in their share.

The answer is Solomon. Verse 45 says the service was done "…as David and his son Solomon had prescribed." A father and son both had a hand in how this service was set up. Solomon is the son the verse names.

The answer is True. Verse 47 says, "…in the days of Zerubbabel and Nehemiah, all Israel contributed the daily portions for the singers and gatekeepers." All Israel pitched in. Everybody had a hand in supporting the ones who served.
The answer is Aaron. Verse 47 says the Levites "…set aside daily portions for the descendants of Aaron." Aaron was Moses' brother (Exodus 4:14). The portions passed along from one group to the next.
